    To beginSeville flamenco party garlic prawnsGarlic and chilli prawns sizzled in olive oil with smoked paprika, parsley, lemon and crusty breadHow to make it600g green prawns, peeled, tails on1/2 tsp salt125ml olive oil6 garlic cloves, thinly sliced1 tsp chilli flakes1 tsp smoked paprika1/2 cup flat-leaf parsley, chopped1 lemon, halved1 baguettePat the prawns dry and season with the salt.Warm the olive oil with the garlic and chilli flakes in a wide pan over low heat until the garlic is pale gold.Turn the heat up, add the prawns and smoked paprika and cook, turning once, until just pink.Stir through the parsley, squeeze over the lemon and serve in the pan with torn baguette.Randwick race day sausage rollsPork and fennel sausage rolls in flaky puff pastry with sesame seeds and tomato sauceHow to make it500g pork mince1 onion, finely grated1 tsp fennel seeds, toasted and crushed1/2 cup fresh breadcrumbs1 egg, for the filling1 tsp salt1/2 tsp black pepper3 sheets of frozen puff pastry, thawed1 egg, beaten, for brushing1 tbsp sesame seeds1/2 cup tomato sauceHeat the oven to 200°C. Mix the mince with the onion, fennel, breadcrumbs, egg for the filling, salt and pepper.Cut each pastry sheet in half, lay a log of filling along each strip, roll up and seal underneath.Chill the logs so they cut cleanly.Brush with the beaten egg, sprinkle with sesame seeds and cut each log into four.Bake until puffed and deep golden.Rest, then serve with the tomato sauce.Sydney rock oysters with lemonAmbrose's day at the races. Nyah has an earpiece in.How to make itA house standard, not part of tonight's cook.Main courseSydney Harbour barramundi with salsa verdeCrisp-skinned barramundi on crushed lemon potatoes with parsley, mint and caper salsa verdeHow to make it800g baby potatoes1 cup flat-leaf parsley leaves1/2 cup mint leaves2 tbsp capers1 garlic clove1 tsp dijon mustard1 lemon, juiced, for the salsa verde125ml extra virgin olive oil2 tbsp olive oil, for the potatoes1 lemon, zested, for the potatoes4 barramundi fillets, skin on, about 180g each1 tbsp olive oil, for the fish1 tsp saltBoil the potatoes in salted water until tender.Finely chop the parsley, mint, capers and garlic and stir with the mustard, lemon juice, extra virgin olive oil and a pinch of salt.Drain the potatoes and crush lightly with the olive oil, lemon zest and salt. Keep warm.Score the fish skin, pat dry and season with salt.Cook the fish skin side down in the hot oil, pressing flat, until crisp, then flip to finish.Serve the fish on the potatoes with the salsa verde spooned over.Ambrose's Bare Island lambAmbrose's hideout in the old fort on Bare Island, out in Botany BayHow to make it2 lamb racks, 8 cutlets each1 bunch rosemary3 garlic cloves2 tbsp olive oil800g small potatoes300g frozen peas1 bunch mint20g butter150ml red wine200ml beef stockBoil the potatoes for 18 minutes, drain and crush with a little oil.Rub the lamb with chopped rosemary, garlic, oil and salt, sear fat side down, then roast at 200°C for 20 minutes. Rest for 10 minutes.Pour the wine into the roasting pan, bubble on the stove, add the stock and reduce for 5 minutes.Cook the peas for 3 minutes and crush with the butter and chopped mint.Cut into cutlets and serve on the potatoes and peas with the jus.DessertSydney summer pavlovaPavlova for the Sydney holiday Ethan and Nyah earn, with cream, mango, kiwifruit and passionfruitHow to make it4 egg whites220g caster sugar2 tsp cornflour1 tsp white vinegar1 tsp vanilla extract300ml thickened cream1 tbsp icing sugar1 mango, sliced2 kiwifruits, peeled and sliced4 passionfruitsHeat the oven to 150°C and draw a 20cm circle on baking paper on a tray.Whisk the egg whites to soft peaks, then add the caster sugar a spoonful at a time and whisk until thick and glossy.Fold in the cornflour, vinegar and vanilla and spread inside the circle with a slight hollow.Turn the oven to 120°C and bake.Turn the oven off and cool the pavlova inside with the door ajar.Whip the cream with the icing sugar.Pile the cream on the pavlova and top with mango, kiwifruit and passionfruit pulp.From the trolleySeville sherry cobblerFino for Nyah's job in Seville, shaken with orange, lemon and syrup over crushed ice, raspberries and mintHow to make it60g caster sugar60ml hot water240ml fino sherry1 orange, juiced1 lemon, juiced4 cups crushed ice1 orange, cut into half wheels125g raspberries4 mint sprigsStir the sugar into the hot water until dissolved, then cool.Shake the sherry, orange juice, lemon juice and syrup hard with ice, in two batches.Strain into four glasses packed with crushed ice.Garnish with orange half wheels, raspberries and mint.Hunter Valley semillonPoured at the races.
